questions.question:
Choose the correct sentence.

(a) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(b) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(c) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(d) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
options: (a) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(b) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(c) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
(d) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.
questions.answer: (a) She has lived in London for five years, but she hasn't got used to the weather.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense?
options: I haven't seen him since last week.
I didn't see him since last week.
I haven't seen him for last week.
I haven't seen him in last week.
questions.answer: I haven't seen him since last week.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'If I _____ more time, I would have finished the report.'
Which modal verb is used to express possibility in the past?
Select the correct form: 'He prefers _____ coffee, but I like tea.'
Which sentence correctly uses comparatives?
options: This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting from that one.
This book is more interesting than that one.
This book is more interesting then that one.
questions.answer: This book is more interesting than that one.

questions.question: Choose the correct conditional sentence: 'We _____ to the cinema if we weren't so tired.'

options: I remember to see that film.
